bio:
The Prindle Genealogy (1906, p.41) confirms James Prindle b. 1736, m. 'Anar' Turner, d. Newtown 1800, and a 'James Jr.' in 1771, but lists no children. FamilySearch assigns him children James (c1754), David (1757), Benjamin (1764), Samuel (c1767) and Hannah (1773) - exactly the Orange Co. sibling set plus militia private Benjamin. Note a James Jr. c.1754 predates the 1759 marriage.

Two Newtown records attached to his FamilySearch profile can now be cited directly. The Newtown church marriage register records 'James Prindle & Anar Turner both of Newtown' married on 22 January 1759 ([R4-S1]), matching the Prindle Genealogy. The Barbour Collection slip abstracted from Newtown Vital Records vol. 2 p.172 reads 'PRINDLE, James, d. Dec. 9, 1800' ([R4-S2]) - December, where the Prindle Genealogy and FamilySearch have 9 November. The 1759 marriage date means that two of the five children FamilySearch assigns to him and Anar (James c.1754 and David 1757) were born before the marriage; they could only be his by an unrecorded earlier wife, or are misattributed. Samuel (c.1767) remains a possible son but is not documented as such.
sources: [R4-S1] Newtown, Conn., church register of marriages, 1759 (Connecticut, Church Records 1660-1955; FS index ark 1:1:QGR1-ZV9P; image attached to tree L8MP-W4X) (primary) https://ancestors.familysearch.org/service/tree/tree-data/published/sources/L8MP-W4X/images/i/2/image.jpg

[R4-S2] Barbour Collection slip, Newtown Vital Records vol. 2 p.172 (Connecticut, Vital Records Prior to 1850; FS index ark 1:1:QPSF-C8RP) (derivative) https://ancestors.familysearch.org/service/tree/tree-data/published/sources/L8MP-W4X/images/i/1/image.jpg
